sections.text: So shall thy action be attended by no result, either good or bad; but through the spirit of renunciation thou shalt come to Me and be free.
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः।
I am the same to all beings. I favour none, and I hate none. But those who worship Me devotedly, they live in Me, and I in them.
Even the most sinful, if he worship Me with his whole heart, shalt be considered righteous, for he is treading the right path.

Obviously we have seen, as Bhagavan said, a royal secret, a grand secret is something which is very close to us but we fail to recognize. Therefore its a secret. So the first declaration in this chapter, Bhagawan says that even though I pervade this entire Jagat, the universe, this creation, in my unmanifest form, all the beings dwell in me, but I dont dwell in them.
They are in me, but Im not in them. Which is obviously quite contrary to what we typically have learned all our life through all religions saying, Bhagwan, the Lord is within you. Here he said, even though I pervade the entire universe in my unmanifest form, I do not dwell in them, they dwell in Me.
Then he even further clarifies in saying, but in reality, they are also not in me. In other words, if we can take it on its face value, if we say we are in him, obviously we are influencing his being. All my qualities of limitedness and imperfection will affect Him.
And therefore he says, in reality, even they are not in Me. None of the qualities we see in this world, in the things and beings, Bhagavan Siddi does not exist in me. All the imperfections we see in this world, which we constantly wonder why Lord created this world like that.
And he says, it is not in Me. And then obviously we have continued to discuss this, the relationship of this creation and the Lord self. And he says, even though this world is created by my maya, I am the efficient cause for this world and I am also the material cause for this world.
And therefore everything comes out of me and everything goes back to me. Because there is no nothing other than him existed before this creation was created. Then nothing will exist after this creation will be dissolved.
All that was there was his own self. So Bhagavan said, the relationship, less relationship between the prakriti, the world, the manifest world as we know, and the unmanifest self which he says pervades entire Jagat, is that of a non existent relationship. But we have created this relationship.
So then we have understood that everything which we do is because of the Lords presence. As long as Im conscious, I can act in this world. So Bhagavan said that everything you do eventually comes to me.
Im the only enjoyer. consciousness is the only enjoyer in any being. Because only time we enjoy or suffer is when we are conscious about it. So we have seen that relationship.
The Bhagavan says, everything comes out of me. Everything dissolves in me. Everything is possible because of me.
Everything can be done only with my presence. However, because of our desires and wrong identification with this limited self, we create our own world of actions and our own world of worship. Depending on my desires, I worship the Lord of my heart.
I put my efforts into the field where I want success. Bhagavan says, those who apply their efforts to fulfill their desires will be blessed to get their desires fulfilled by me. So then we have seen in detail that the worshipers of the Devas goes to the Devas.
Worshipper of the Bhutas goes to Bhutas. Worshipper of the Pitrus go to the Pitras. Deva, as we say Diva is to illumine which relates to our senses.
So whoever perceives the visual arts, excel in visual arts. Whoever perceives performing arts, excels in performing arts. So we know in this world we can prove from our own experience that wherever I put my efforts, wherever I identify myself, thats the field Ill excel.
That the success I will receive. Same way we see the Pitruloka, the cultural heritage of our ancestors. Those who value that and put efforts in that, they will achieve that.
Bhutas we have seen is the physical sciences. Science of this manifest world is Bhuta. Those who pursue that, they excel in that.
But see, all these successes are finite in nature, exist in time and space. And once you achieve that success, enjoy the fruits of it. You to come back to pursue the next desire which you have and the next success you want.
So this is the coming and going which Bhagavad Gita and Upanishad describe. We constantly achieve, things, enjoy it, come back, strive for something else, achieve that, come back, strive for something else. But Bhagavan said, the one who worships me -- and we have seen, worship is devotion, devotion is love for the Divine, love is identification -- one who starts identifying with that eternal self will achieve me.
That we have seen in the last three verses. Verse 26 actually says Patram Puspam falam toyam Yomi bhakta prayachati Tadaham bhakt Apurhat asnami prayatat Manaha. Whatsoever my devotee offer me with devotion, I accept that.
Thats good enough for me. You really dont have to have elaborate resources to worship Lord. And as we discussed last time, it takes away any excuse that I may have.
Look, Im not strong enough. I dont have enough strength or I dont have enough wealth. But once it is whatever you can offer from my own garden, whatever you can pluck and give it back to me, Ill be happy simply because I see your devotion.
What hes looking for is your intention, your devotion and your attitude. So the next verse 27 says, Yat karosi yatasnasi yat johosi dadasiyat. Now here comes the prescription.
We have seen in theory what is our relationship to the Lord? What can we do to remove this parallax between myself and his self? And then we may have an excuse saying, but Im not capable of doing so. There is a very simple method. And you will not need anything more than what you already have.
All you have to do is change your attitude in what you do. Yat Karoshi -- whatever you do, no matter who you are: a cobbler, a weaver, a doctor, an engineer, a president -- whatever you are, whatever you are doing. Yat Ashnasi -- whatever you are receiving, eating.
View and says eating is not only what we eat through our mouth but anything we take in through our eyes, ears, and all the senses. Yat Juhoshi -- whatever you offer back to the world. Yat Dadasi -- whatever you give as charity.
Yat Tapasyasi -- whatever discipline you are following. We all follow some discipline -- I have to get up in the morning, do this, do that. We follow discipline to achieve anything.
Whatever discipline you are following to achieve what you are pursuing -- it is that simple: do not do it for yourself. Right now we are doing it for ourselves. It is very clear in my mind why I am doing this.
Rajan, why are you doing this? Well, because I want to do this. Rajan, why dont you do this? Because I dont want to do that. Its as simple as that.
So we know very clearly that all my actions are for me. For me to achieve what I want. Bhagavan says, just change that attitude and have that attitude that Im offering.
All my actions, all my charities, all my disciplines, all that Im receiving is to him. Because without his presence as the consciousness in me, none of these activities are possible in the first place. So who am I to take credit now when I say who am I? As I said I reside in my ego.
That I which resides in my ego -- if it gives up that I and says, Im only possible as long as this consciousness functions through me, and I do not know where this consciousness comes from; it must be my Lords presence -- then I offer all my actions to him. Bhagavan says, you will achieve myself. So thats a simple prescription.
Do not change anything that you are doing except change your attitude that youre not doing it for yourself, youre doing it for him. Therefore, when you enjoy something, hes the enjoyer. When you suffer, hes the sufferer.
You achieve something, hes the achiever. When you fail somewhere, he bears the failure. Shubha Ashubha Phalaih Evam Mokshyase -- thus you shall be freed from this bondage of Shubha and Ashubha, this bondage of labeling things as good for me or not good for me. When something good for me happens, Im very proud.
When something good doesnt happen for me, I blame everybody else other than me. He should have done this. Why didnt he tell me that? Why didnt he do that? We find everybody responsible except me.
Also it creates negative impression on my mind. Well, next time I never want to do that. I went to this organization for volunteer my services and they were not appreciative at all.
I will never do that again. So I lost a chance of doing something good in life. That bondage which is created by the impressions on my mind -- by perceiving this is good for me and this is bad for me -- you will be freed from.
You will then see clearly, without having a cataract in your vision. I went to the doctor a few weeks ago and he said, Open your right eye. I could barely see anything, completely fuzzy. I said, Im fine. He said, thats because your left eye is taking over.
And he said, thank God you dont have cataract in both eyes. Thats exactly what he told me. So you can imagine if you have a cataract in a vision in both your eyes, the world will be very fuzzy.
And Bhagavan said, thats where we are Right now. Because if one eye we see Subha, other we see a Subha and we have a very distorted view of this world. But once we are freed from that, you have 2020 vision of this world.
And then you will be doing exactly what is appropriate at an appropriate time. And when you do that, you know what you will achieve? So youll be freed from by changing your attitude about everything you do. From doing it for myself to doing it for his self, I will be freed from the bondage of this is good and this is bad.
Whatever the results come from my actions, Ill say, lord, you gave me this Buddhi to do this and I did that. Now this is what you are giving me as a prasad. Im sure you know what youre doing.
Then this must be good for me. Im accepting it and Im moving forward. Next step, Sannyasa, Yoga Yuktatma, Vimukto Mam Upeshasi.
You will become Sannyasa and Yoga Yuktatma. We have learned these terms in previous chapters that should I be a Sanyasi or should I be any yogi? He says sannyasi is the one who has given up the sense of agency. I am the doer that agency.
One who gives up, he is called Sannyasi., not the one who wears the saffron robe and has a long beard. One who has given up the sense of agency that I am the doer is a Sannyasi. The yogi is the one who has given up the desire for the results of the actions.
One who is given the Karma Phala is the yogi. You are established in Yoga if you have no particular desire for particular results. I will do my actions because I am not the Karma Faladatta.
I am never the actor is never in control of its results. Its always somebody else. You present a song, you present a performance.
Its not who you are going to applaud. Other people are going to applaud or other people are going to throw stones at you.

Verse 28 promises liberation from shubha-ashubha-phalaih - the bondage created by labeling results as good or bad. Like having cataracts in both eyes, we see a fuzzy, distorted world when we constantly sort experiences into favorable and unfavorable. The sannyasa-yoga described here is not about external renunciation but internal freedom: sannyasi is one who gives up the sense of doership; yogi is one who gives up attachment to specific results. When both are achieved, you act with full engagement yet remain untouched by outcomes - not through suppression but through understanding.
Samoham sarva-bhuteshu (verse 29) - I am the same to all beings. The Divine has no favorites. Like a parent whose love for all children is equal (even if one visits more often), Krishnas relationship with every being is identical. The difference we experience is not in His giving but in our receiving. Ye bhajanti tu mam bhaktya, mayi te teshu chapy aham - those who worship with devotion dwell in Him, and He in them. The intimacy is not one-sided; it is mutual. You are not reaching toward a distant God; you are recognizing the God who has never left.
Verse 30 offers radical hope: Api chet su-duracharo - even the worst sinner, if they worship with undivided devotion, should be considered righteous (sadhur eva). This is not endorsement of wrongdoing but acknowledgment that right resolve changes everything. Your past does not define your future; your present orientation does. Today, release any sense that you are disqualified from spiritual progress due to past mistakes. Ask: Am I now, in this moment, rightly resolved toward truth? That is the only question that matters.
